paragraphs.text: XIV.A. After Landing, Parking, & Securing
Introduction
How
Parking
Select a parking location and heading that avoids the propeller and jet blast from other planes
Also ensure you are not parked in a way that will blast other aircraft
Park heading into the wind, if possible
Hand signals may be used if ramp personnel are available – be familiar
After stopping, roll forward slightly to straighten the nosewheel
Engine Shutdown 										AI.XIV.A.K1
A flight is not complete until the engine is shut down and the airplane is secured
Once stopped, set the parking brake
Common practice: With the engine running, move the ignition from BOTH to OFF and back to BOTH
Ensures mags are properly grounded
Follow the procedures outlined on the manufacturer’s checklist
Read each item aloud and perform the task (Read and Do)
CE: Hazards resulting from failure to follow recommended procedures 			AI.XIV.A.K3
RM: Deplaning Passengers 									AI.XIV.A.R3
Ensure passengers understand the safe procedures for exiting the airplane (after engine shutdown)
Ensure passengers are aware of potential hazards nearby – other aircraft starting, taxiing, etc.
Do not let the passengers disembark until required checklists are complete & safety precautions met
Postflight Inspection 									AI.XIV.A.K1
Postflight Inspection
Check the general condition of the aircraft
Inspect the outside for any damage that may have occurred
Look for leaks, streaks, stains
Check oil, and other required fluids and replenish as necessary
Document all Discrepancies 								AI.XIV.A.K2
Don’t leave the problem for someone else
Allows maintenance to fix issues
If not fixed, it informs the next pilot of the issue so they can make an informed go/no go decision
Allows pilots/maintenance to see trends/repeating problems
Fuel the Airplane
If another flight is planned, the tanks should be filled based on that flight’s fuel requirements
If the aircraft is going to be inactive, fill the tanks to prevent water condensation from forming
Securing the Aircraft 									AI.XIV.A.K1
An essential part of every flight
Remove personal belongings
Verify the nosewheel is straight
Parking Brake/Tiedown/Chocked, as necessary
Flight controls secured, gust locks
Covered (airframe, propeller, shades, inlet covers, pitot covers, etc.) and/or hangered
Windows closed
Locked
Any other requirements for your aircraft
RM: Airport Specific Security Procedures 							AI.XIV.A.R2
Address any specific procedures (hours of operation, gates, codes, other requirements)
CE: Poor planning/procedure or faulty judgment in postflight procedures 	AI.XIV.A.K3
Be aware of the parking areas (ramps space, FBOs, etc.) at the destination
RM: Activities & Distractions 								AI.XIV.A.R1
Taxiing and parking around buildings, people, etc. is no time to be distracted (sterile flight deck)
Follow all checklist(s) step by step, and ensure the airplane is left in a safe condition for the next flight
Do not skip the postflight inspection and assume the next pilot will catch any issues in their preflight
If a discrepancy is noted, attempt to have the issue inspected and fixed prior to the next flight
If unsure about something, ask (avoid faulty judgment)
Don’t assume “it will be OK”
Don’t make a safety decision for the next pilot – inform them and let them make the decision
Verify with the POH, a flight instructor, Chief Pilot, maintenance, etc.
Leaving the airplane in an unsafe place, condition, or situation can result in damage and/or injuries
Conclusion:
Brief review of the main points

paragraphs.text: XIV.A. After Landing, Parking, & Securing
References: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3), POH/AFM
Instructor Notes:
Introduction:
Attention
Interesting fact or attention-grabbing story

Have you ever forgotten to turn something off after a flight? Leaving certain things running can be dangerous or costly. Properly securing an airplane isn’t important just to save on costs though, weather, and other situations can cause damage and/or injuries.
Overview
Review Objectives and Elements/Key ideas
What
Postflight procedures are completed at the end of the flight when the airplane is parked, shut down, and properly secured.
Why
The postflight is just as important as preflight in maintaining the aircraft and keeping it in a safe condition for the next flight.
How:
Parking
Select a parking location and heading that avoids the propeller/jet blast of other planes
Also ensure you are not parked in a way that will blast other aircraft
Be considerate of others
Whenever possible, park heading into the wind
Often, your choice is limited to designated parking spots and tie downs - work with what you have
Hand signals may be used if ramp personnel are available – be familiar
After stopping, allow the airplane to roll forward to straighten the nosewheel
Engine Shutdown 			AI.XIV.A.K1
Follow the procedures in the manufacturer’s checklist for shutting down and securing
Read each item aloud and perform the task
CE: Hazards resulting from failure to follow recommended procedures
Like always, it is very important to follow the manufacturer’s checklist
Follow the published procedures to avoid missing important steps/creating an unsafe situation
Set the parking brake to keep the plane from moving
*Checklist:
*While the engine is running, move the ignition switch from BOTH to OFF and back to BOTH
This ensures the magnetos are properly grounded at every engine shutdown
Once the engine is shutdown, secure the flight deck
Gather belongings and complete any securing checklist items (control lock, windows, shades, etc.)
*Double check that the master is off, the magnetos are off and the key has been removed, electrical equipment is off, the trim is neutral, flaps are up, and the mixture and throttle are idle
RM: Deplaning Passengers 										AI.XIV.A.R3
Ensure passengers understand the safe procedures for exiting the airplane (after engine shutdown)
Inform them when it is safe to unbuckle and exit
Be aware of potential hazards nearby – other aircraft starting, taxiing in/out, etc.
Ensure the passengers know where to go to prevent wandering into an unsafe situation
The aircraft should be shutdown/configured to allow for safe movement of passengers
Chock to prevent movement
Do not let the passengers disembark until required checklists are complete and safety precautions met
Postflight Inspection 										AI.XIV.A.K1
Postflight Inspection
Check the general condition of the aircraft
Inspect the outside for any damage that may have occurred
Look for leaks, streaks, stains
Check oil, and other required fluids and replenish as necessary
Document all Discrepancies 									AI.XIV.A.K2
Don’t leave the problem for someone else
Not only dangerous, but just rude
Allows maintenance to fix issues
If not fixed, informs the next pilot of the discrepancies
They can make an informed go/no go decision
Can see trends/repeating problems
Fuel the Airplane
If another flight is planned, the tanks should be filled based on that flight’s fuel requirements
If the aircraft is going to be inactive, fill the tanks to prevent water condensation from forming
Refueling Procedures
Ensure the ramp personnel use the proper type/grade of fuel
If possible, be there when the fueling takes place to ensure the proper grade
Always check/drain the fuel prior to the next flight to be sure the proper fuel was used, and water/sediment hasn’t accumulated since the last flight
Securing the Aircraft 										AI.XIV.A.K1
An essential part of every flight
Remove personal belongings
Verify the nosewheel is straight
Tiedown/chocked
Tie downs may vary significantly between chains and well-worn ropes
Chains are not flexible and therefore should not be made taught to prevent structural damage
Ropes are flexible and may be reasonably cinched to the tie down rings
Brakes should be set based on local procedures – some request the brakes set, some don’t
Flight controls secured, gust locks
Covered (airframe, propeller, shades, inlet covers, pitot covers, etc.) and/or hangered
Windows closed
Locked
Any other requirements for your aircraft
RM: Airport Specific Security Procedures 							AI.XIV.A.R2
Address any specific procedures (hours of operation, gates, codes, other requirements)
CE: Poor planning, improper procedure, or faulty judgment in performance of postflight procedures
Be aware of the parking areas (ramps space, FBOs, etc.) at the destination
If necessary, contact the FBO or parking management to verify the location and any procedures
RM: Activities & Distractions 									AI.XIV.A.R1
Taxiing and parking around buildings, people, etc. is no time to be distracted (sterile flight deck)
Follow all checklist(s) step by step, and ensure the airplane is left in a safe condition for the next flight
Don’t operate by memory
If distracted, restart the checklist to ensure completion
Activities other than those associated with landing, parking & securing should be delayed
Do not skip the postflight inspection, assuming the next pilot will catch any issues in their preflight
They might not catch the issue which could be very hazardous
The issue could have been found and possibly fixed prior to them showing up (be considerate)
If a discrepancy is noted, attempt to have the issue inspected/fixed prior to the next flight
If unsure about something, ask (avoid faulty judgement)
Don’t assume “it will be OK”
Don’t make a safety decision for the next pilot – inform them and let them make the decision
Verify with the POH, an instructor, Chief Pilot, maintenance, etc.
Leaving the airplane in an unsafe place, condition, or situation can result in damage and/or injuries
Common Errors: 											AI.XIV.A.K3
Hazards resulting from failure to follow recommended procedures
Poor planning, improper procedure, or faulty judgment in performance of postflight procedures
Conclusion:
Brief review of the main points
When parking and shutting down the airplane it is very important to follow the manufacturer’s established guidelines to ensure everything is properly shut down and secured.
